target.rawQueryText:

  SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, r.value AS value,
         LAG(r.value) OVER (ORDER BY r.ts) AS previous,

  WHERE s.key = 'go'
)
WHERE value = 1 AND (previous IS NULL OR previous <> 1)
  AND time BETWEEN $__from/1000.0 AND $__to/1000.0
ORDER BY time

SELECT time, text FROM (
  SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, r.value AS value,
         LAG(r.value) OVER (ORDER BY r.ts) AS previous,
         'Charge started' AS text
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  WHERE s.key = 'bms_state_charge'
)
WHERE value = 1 AND (previous IS NULL OR previous <> 1)
  AND time BETWEEN $__from/1000.0 AND $__to/1000.0
ORDER BY time

SELECT time, text FROM (
  SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, r.value AS value,
         LAG(r.value) OVER (ORDER BY r.ts) AS previous,

)

description: Post-ride summary: distance, speed, power, energy, peak temperatures, elevation and bike state for one ride.

options.content:
Ride telemetry from CAN `0x104`/`0x105`/`0x108` (speed, odometer, motor), `0x200`-`0x206` (BMS),
`0x10A` (energy and range), `0x410` (GPS via the Connectivity Hub) and the OBD poller.

**What the 2026-08-02 capture contains.** A short lap and then a garage session. Several decoders
only came online after the lap, so the tiles reading them cannot describe it: `odometer_can_km`,
`speed_can_kmh`, `motor_rpm_can` and `motor_temp_c` all have a handful of samples, none of them
during the ride. `trip_km` is the one distance signal with samples through it: +0.2 km across the whole
capture, of which 0.1 km falls inside the lap itself — it only resolves to 0.1 km and logged
3 rows during the lap, so read it as coarse. That is why the Trip meter tile exists next to
Distance.

**What is empty, and why.** Elevation, Elevation range and Highest point draw nothing because
`gps_fix` is 0 for the whole capture. The bike was in a garage: `gps_altitude_m` sat at a
placeholder 0 m and `gps_lat`/`gps_lon` were never written at all. Those three panels are gated on
the fix rather than plotting the placeholder, so an empty chart there means "no fix" - which the
'GPS fix over time' lane at the bottom of the Position row states outright. That is the signal being absent,
not a broken query.

**Reading the panels.** Values are logged on change with a per-signal deadband, so a flat stretch
means "unchanged", not "missing". Every series uses stepAfter with spanNulls on for that reason.

panels.description: MAX - MIN of odometer_can_km over the selected range. Chosen over the other three distance signals: it is the CAN 0x104 lifetime odometer at 0.1 km and it agrees with the hub's odometer_km, which only has 1 km resolution. OBD dist_since_clear_km sits ~4 km higher because it counts from the last DTC clear, not from zero. Reads 0.0 km in the 2026-08-02 capture: the 0x104 decoder only came online after the lap, so use the trip meter tile for that ride. Values are logged on change with a per-signal deadband, so a gap means "unchanged", not "missing". stepAfter + spanNulls therefore draws exactly what was recorded; linear interpolation would invent samples that were never on the bus.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT MAX(r.ts)/1000.0 AS time, MAX(r.value) - MIN(r.value) AS "Distance"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'odometer_can_km' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
HAVING COUNT(*) > 0

panels.title: Distance

panels.description: Last odometer_can_km in range. Unit is a fixed km suffix on purpose: Grafana's built-in lengthkm applies SI prefixes and renders 17042 km as "17 Mm".

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, r.value AS "Odometer"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'odometer_can_km' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: Odometer

panels.description: MAX - MIN of trip_km, the hub's own trip counter at 0.1 km. Cross-check on the Distance tile, and the only distance signal with samples through the 2026-08-02 lap: +0.2 km across the whole capture, 0.1 km of it inside the lap window, off 3 rows at 0.1 km resolution. Its absolute reading is a running counter that has not been reset, so only the delta means anything.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT MAX(r.ts)/1000.0 AS time, MAX(r.value) - MIN(r.value) AS "Trip meter"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'trip_km' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
HAVING COUNT(*) > 0

panels.title: Trip meter

panels.description: MAX of speed_kmh, the OBD-polled speed at ~2 Hz. The CAN speed (speed_can_kmh, 0x104) is finer but its decoder only started after the 2026-08-02 lap, so OBD is the one with ride coverage. Both are drawn on the Speed panel below.

targets.rawQueryText:

FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'speed_kmh' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
HAVING COUNT(*) > 0

panels.title: Top speed

panels.description: MAX of motor_power_kw (CAN, 0.05 kW deadband). Fixed kW suffix rather than Grafana's kwatt, which would re-scale 0.6 kW to "600 W" mid-column.

targets.rawQueryText:

FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id

panels.title: Peak motor power

Values are logged on change with a per-signal deadband, so a gap means "unchanged", not "missing". stepAfter + spanNulls therefore draws exactly what was recorded; linear interpolation would invent samples that were never on the bus.

Values are logged on change with a per-signal deadband, so a gap means "unchanged", not "missing". stepAfter + spanNulls therefore draws exactly what was recorded; linear interpolation would invent samples that were never on the bus.

panels.description: First minus last residual_energy_wh in range, i.e. what the pack lost. Goes negative if the range also contains a charge.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT MAX(r.ts)/1000.0 AS time,
  (SELECT f.value FROM reading f JOIN signal fs ON fs.id = f.signal_id
   WHERE fs.key = 'residual_energy_wh' AND f.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to ORDER BY f.ts ASC LIMIT 1)
  - (SELECT l.value FROM reading l JOIN signal ls ON ls.id = l.signal_id
     WHERE ls.key = 'residual_energy_wh' AND l.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to ORDER BY l.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  AS "Energy used"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'residual_energy_wh' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
HAVING COUNT(*) > 0

panels.title: Energy used

panels.description: First minus last soc in range. SOC is a 1 % integer, so a short lap can read 0.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT MAX(r.ts)/1000.0 AS time,
  (SELECT f.value FROM reading f JOIN signal fs ON fs.id = f.signal_id
   WHERE fs.key = 'soc' AND f.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to ORDER BY f.ts ASC LIMIT 1)
  - (SELECT l.value FROM reading l JOIN signal ls ON ls.id = l.signal_id
     WHERE ls.key = 'soc' AND l.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to ORDER BY l.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  AS "SOC used"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'soc' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
HAVING COUNT(*) > 0

panels.title: SOC used

panels.description: Last range_km: the bike's own prediction of distance left, not a computed figure. It reacts hard to recent riding style, so treat it as the dash reading rather than a measurement.

panels.title: Range remaining

panels.description: Last km_per_kwh as reported by the bike. It recomputes continuously and swings hard at low speed - it goes negative under regen and reads -5.36 at the end of the 2026-08-02 capture - so it is worth reading at the end of a ride, not mid-lap.

targets.rawQueryText:

FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'km_per_kwh' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to

panels.title: Energy remaining

panels.description: inst_consumption_wh carries a 10 Wh deadband because it is otherwise the chattiest signal on the bus. Parked it sits at 0. Values are logged on change with a per-signal deadband, so a gap means "unchanged", not "missing". stepAfter + spanNulls therefore draws exactly what was recorded; linear interpolation would invent samples that were never on the bus.

panels.description: Battery, inverter, motor and coolant-outlet temperature on one axis. The battery and motor signals carry deadbands of about half a degree, the coolant probe 0.05 C, which is why the coolant trace has far more steps. FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'batt_temp_hi' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to

FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'inverter_igbt_max_c' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to

WHERE s.key = 'coolant_out' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to AND r.value BETWEEN -20 AND 100

panels.title: Ride temperatures

panels.description: Last gps_fix, the 2-bit fix field out of CAN 0x410. 0 means no fix and is the only value confirmed on the bench; 1-3 are shown raw. In a garage this reads "no fix", gps_altitude_m is a placeholder 0 and gps_lat/gps_lon are never written at all, which is why the elevation panels below are gated on this signal instead of plotting the zero.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, r.value AS "GPS fix"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'gps_fix' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: GPS fix

panels.description: Last gps_satellites. The decoder only publishes a position with a fix and at least 4 satellites, so this is the number to look at when the elevation panels are empty.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, r.value AS "Satellites"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'gps_satellites' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: Satellites

panels.description: MAX - MIN of gps_altitude_m across rows whose most recent gps_fix is non-zero: the span between the lowest and highest point, not cumulative climb. A loop that climbs and descends the same 400 m twice reads 400 m here, and summing the positive deltas instead would sum GPS jitter into a fake climb against the 1 m deadband. With no fix the query returns nothing and the tile says so rather than reporting a 0 m spread from the placeholder altitude.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT MAX(r.ts)/1000.0 AS time, MAX(r.value) - MIN(r.value) AS "Elevation range"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'gps_altitude_m' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
  AND COALESCE((
    SELECT f.value FROM reading f JOIN signal fs ON fs.id = f.signal_id
    WHERE fs.key = 'gps_fix' AND f.ts <= r.ts + 2000
    ORDER BY f.ts DESC LIMIT 1
  ), 0) > 0
HAVING COUNT(*) > 0

panels.title: Elevation range

panels.description: MAX of gps_altitude_m, same fix gate as Elevation range.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT MAX(r.ts)/1000.0 AS time, MAX(r.value) AS "Highest point"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'gps_altitude_m' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
  AND COALESCE((
    SELECT f.value FROM reading f JOIN signal fs ON fs.id = f.signal_id
    WHERE fs.key = 'gps_fix' AND f.ts <= r.ts + 2000
    ORDER BY f.ts DESC LIMIT 1
  ), 0) > 0
HAVING COUNT(*) > 0

panels.title: Highest point

panels.description: gps_altitude_m, plotted only where the most recent gps_fix is non-zero. The gate looks back past the start of the range on purpose, so a fix acquired earlier still counts. Empty means no fix, not a missing decoder: the 2026-08-02 capture was made in a garage where the altitude sat at a placeholder 0 m. Values are logged on change with a per-signal deadband, so a gap means "unchanged", not "missing". stepAfter + spanNulls therefore draws exactly what was recorded; linear interpolation would invent samples that were never on the bus.

defaults.noValue: no GPS fix in this range

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, r.value AS "Elevation"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'gps_altitude_m' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
  AND COALESCE((
    SELECT f.value FROM reading f JOIN signal fs ON fs.id = f.signal_id
    WHERE fs.key = 'gps_fix' AND f.ts <= r.ts + 2000
    ORDER BY f.ts DESC LIMIT 1
  ), 0) > 0
ORDER BY r.ts

panels.title: Elevation

panels.description: The gate the Elevation panel above runs on. An empty elevation chart with a red "no fix" bar here means the receiver never had a fix, which is a different thing from a missing decoder or a broken query.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time,
  CASE WHEN r.value <> 0 THEN 'fix' ELSE 'no fix' END AS "GPS fix"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'gps_fix' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts

panels.title: GPS fix over time

panels.description: Boolean CAN signals as lanes. Each stored row is a change, so a lane holds its value until the next row; spanNulls is on for the same reason. In the 2026-08-02 capture these decoders only started after the lap, so the lanes are short.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time,
  CASE WHEN r.value <> 0 THEN 'yes' ELSE 'no' END AS "Key on"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'key_on' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts

SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time,
  CASE WHEN r.value <> 0 THEN 'yes' ELSE 'no' END AS "GO"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'go' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts

SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time,
  CASE WHEN r.value <> 0 THEN 'yes' ELSE 'no' END AS "Moving"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'moving' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts

SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time,
  CASE WHEN r.value <> 0 THEN 'yes' ELSE 'no' END AS "Reverse"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'reverse_gear' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts

SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time,
  CASE WHEN r.value <> 0 THEN 'yes' ELSE 'no' END AS "Brake"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'brake' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts

SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time,
  CASE WHEN r.value <> 0 THEN 'yes' ELSE 'no' END AS "Throttle on"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'throttle_on' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts

panels.title: State

panels.description: Roll and pitch from the VCU's attitude sensor, CAN 0x102 b4-7, in degrees. Roll is positive leaning right; pitch is positive nose-down, i.e. braking. Both are gravity-referenced and not fused with a gyro, so they report the direction of the measured vertical rather than the bike's true attitude: a steady corner reads close to zero, because the bike leans into the resultant, and most of what pitch shows is braking and acceleration rather than gradient. Rows before 2026-08-15 were logged as accel_lateral_raw / accel_frontal_raw — the same angles in units of 0.1°, under a wrong name — so each query divides those by 10 and the history stays continuous across the rename. The axis is soft-limited to at least ±45° so that a parked window cannot autoscale a degree of noise into a dramatic chart; it is deliberately not hard-limited, so the rare atan2 wrap transient (±170° for a few frames after a hard hit) will still stretch it, and is meant to. The full evidence is in src/can/attitude.ts.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, r.value AS "Roll (right +)"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'attitude_roll_deg' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
UNION ALL
SELECT r.ts/1000.0, r.value/10.0
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'accel_lateral_raw' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY 1

SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, r.value AS "Pitch (nose-down +)"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'attitude_pitch_deg' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
UNION ALL
SELECT r.ts/1000.0, r.value/10.0
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'accel_frontal_raw' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY 1
